semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: The term "post-hoc interpretability" emphasizes methods that interpret models after they have been trained. "Model-agnostic interpretability" aligns closely because it refers to methods that apply to any model regardless of its architecture, typically after model training, making it semantically similar to the notion of "post-hoc interpretability."

parent_domains.justification: "Interpretability" is a broad category encompassing various methods and approaches to understanding machine learning models, including post-hoc techniques.
This domain aggregates both interpretability, which includes post-hoc methods, and the broader concept of explainability, making it a parent domain.

closest_parent_domain.justification: "Interpretability" is the most foundational and relevant domain, as it covers all methods to understand machine learning models, directly relating to post-hoc methods.

child_domains.justification: This domain focuses on interpreting models post-training, which fits under "post-hoc interpretability."

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Mechanistic interpretability often aligns with post-hoc methods aiming to understand model behavior after training, making it a closely related sibling domain.
